newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Two killed by stray bullets in Albania.
newsitem.headline: Two killed by stray bullets in Albania.

text.p: Stray bullets killed an eight-year-old girl in the Albanian town of Vlore on Sunday and another victim died in the riot-hit southern town of Gjirokaster, hospital sources said.
They said the girl, who was not named, had not been the target of an attack in the southern Adriatic port of Vlore, where armed rioters have put police and soldiers to flight.
The sources said the bullet either ricocheted off a building or had hit the girl after being fired into the air.
A further 22 people were also treated for wounds at the hospital on Sunday, the sources said.
In Gjirokaster, near the Greek border, one person was killed and two were injured by gunfire and were undergoing surgery, hospital officials said.
"They were all hit by stray bullets for sure," one official said.
Rioters in the town sprayed a police station with bullets from Kalashnikov assault rifles and then set it ablaze, witnesses said.
Police fled as up to 30 masked raiders attacked the building. Flames rose up soon afterwards and the crackle of automatic gunfire mixed with the din of ambulance sirens.

Vlore was the scene on Friday night of the worst violence in two months of unrest in Albania, Europe's poorest state, following the collapse of pyramid savings schemes which had soaked up many people's life savings.
Up to nine people, three of them civilians, were reported killed in the Friday gun battle between demonstrators and Shik secret policemen.
The Albanian parliament on Sunday declared an immediate state of emergency in response to the uprising in Vlore and a string of southern towns.
